lead.headline: Glacial flood kills at least 160 in Nepal, hundreds missing
lead.dek: An ice avalanche dammed and released a Himalayan river; the Trishuli rose 27 feet in half an hour
body: Flash floods tore down the Trishuli river valley on the Nepal-China border Wednesday morning after a glacier collapse sent ice and rock into the Lhende Khola tributary, killing at least 160 people and burying villages in Nepal's Rasuwa and Nuwakot districts in mud. Officials in Nepal reported 403 people missing, among them 341 foreign nationals, and Chinese state media reported 558 missing across the border in Tibet's Gyirong County.

The missing include 133 Indian pilgrims bound for Mount Kailash, 47 Americans and 33 Britons, Nepal's tourism board said. At least 19 bridges and some 25 miles of road were swept away, along with several hydropower projects. The International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development said the Trishuli rose 9 meters — about 27 feet — within half an hour, a speed and magnitude it called exceptional.

Nepal has asked both India and China to help with the rescue, government spokesperson Sasmit Pokharel said, and U.N. teams deployed to what the organization called a massive humanitarian need. It is the second flood on the Lhende Khola in 14 months, a pattern climate specialists tied to increasingly unstable glaciers in a warming Himalaya.

briefs.headline: Meta settles states' child-safety case for up to $17B
briefs.summary: The settlement with 51 states, reached in the Oakland trial's second week, pays out over 10 years and sets a two-hour daily default limit and a midnight-to-6 a.m. block for teen accounts.

briefs.headline: Two Pennsylvania measles deaths are the year's first in U.S.
briefs.summary: Both were unvaccinated Lancaster County residents, the state's first measles deaths in 35 years. Pennsylvania counts 393 cases; the CDC's national count of 2,777 is the highest since 1991.

briefs.headline: ICE sweep nets more than 1,300 arrests in Virginia, Maryland
briefs.summary: The two-week operation announced Monday ran Aug. 1-14 around Washington; about 400 of those arrested had been convicted of or charged with crimes in the U.S., the department said.

briefs.headline: SpaceX plans $100B Louisiana spaceport, its largest yet
briefs.summary: The 125,000-acre Pecan Island site in Vermilion Parish would carry five complexes and 10 pads for southward polar launches, with construction from 2027 and a first Starship flight targeted for 2029.

briefs.headline: Gang leader threatens Kenscoff hostages as toll reaches 47
briefs.summary: The leader known as Izo 2 posted a video vowing to kill more than 50 captives if police strike back; the U.N. said 22 of Sunday's victims were executed in a church compound.

briefs.headline: Tinubu orders manhunt after Nigeria raids kill more than 40
briefs.summary: Gunmen hit four villages in Niger state's Borgu area Friday, attacking mosques during prayers; a local youth leader put abductions as high as 500, a figure not yet verified.

briefs.headline: Projectile disables tanker in Omani waters near Hormuz
briefs.summary: The Monday night strike east of the Musandam Peninsula knocked out the ship's engine room; the crew is safe. The IMO counts 68 such incidents and 20 seafarers killed in six months.

briefs.headline: Palace calls King Harald's condition 'extremely serious'
briefs.summary: Norway's 89-year-old monarch, Europe's oldest reigning sovereign, has been hospitalized since Aug. 17 with hemolytic anemia; Crown Prince Haakon is serving as regent.

briefs.headline: Lottery Commission approves Greenbrier casino license
briefs.summary: Wednesday's vote seats Kennedy Lewis with 51% control and three of five board seats under chairman Lloyd Charles Nathan; the Justice family keeps 49%, with Jill Justice on the board.

briefs.headline: Eagle Horizon to close Boone County mine, cutting 71 jobs
briefs.summary: The WARN notice sets separations for Oct. 11 at the operation near Ashford — miners, electricians, mechanics and foremen among them. The company gave no reason for the closure.

briefs.headline: State's share of Meta settlement to top $114 million
briefs.summary: West Virginia's cut of the multistate child-safety settlement is earmarked for youth mental health services and public education on social media's risks.

regional.item: Marshall moved about 40 students from the six vacated 5th Avenue houses into the downtown DoubleTree through Sept. 9.
Kanawha schools will reword a Hope Scholarship notice to special-education parents after the attorney general said it misstates their rights.

away.item: Three neighbors appealed the $42.7M resort permit for the former Southern Vermont College campus to the Environmental Court on Aug. 11.

hotspots.item: Gauley season opens Sept. 11 — 22 release days from Summersville Dam over six weekends, closing on Bridge Day weekend Oct. 17-18.
Surf City put segment five of the JH Batts multi-use path out to bid Tuesday, with sealed bids due Oct. 12 at the Hampstead municipal complex.

briefs.headline: City weighs whether its grid can carry data centers
briefs.summary: Prince George's roads and utilities date on average to 1982, but B.C. Hydro says transmission capacity exists on a first-come basis as council eyes industrial and data center growth.

briefs.headline: Bald Range fire holds at 25,021 hectares near Summerland
briefs.summary: Weekend rain has kept behaviour down on the fire that has destroyed about 150 structures; evacuation orders remain, and the provincial emergency runs through Saturday.

briefs.headline: Ottawa publishes its list of 700 counter-tariff targets
briefs.summary: The duties of 15% to 50% on $27.6 billion in U.S. goods — steel, dairy, appliances, electronics — take effect Sept. 8, alongside a $7.5 billion support package for workers and businesses.

briefs.headline: Mars' southern interior runs hundreds of degrees hotter
briefs.summary: Gravity data from three orbiters shows the planet's south is 200-400 C warmer inside than its north and partially molten, a Caltech-led team reports in Nature — a clue to its magnetic quirks.

briefs.headline: Fossil wings give voice to a 165-million-year-old forest
briefs.summary: From 20 katydid wings found in Inner Mongolia, researchers reconstructed Jurassic calls — mostly pure 5 kHz tones, with one species singing above 20 kHz, ultrasonic long before bats existed.

briefs.headline: Roman telescope sealed in its fairing for Sunday launch
briefs.summary: NASA's wide-field infrared observatory was encapsulated Aug. 21 and lifts off on a Falcon Heavy from pad 39A at 7:26 a.m. ET Sunday — nine months ahead of its original date.

briefs.headline: AI guides a live brain surgery for the first time in Britain
briefs.summary: A UCL system read the surgical video in real time during a pituitary tumor removal at the National Hospital for Neurology, flagging structures a millimeter from the optic nerves; the patient's sight was saved.

briefs.headline: Amazon closes Mechanical Turk, the AI era's first job board
briefs.summary: The 21-year-old marketplace, which paid cents per task and once counted 500,000 workers labeling the data that trained machine learning, shuts Sept. 30 as that work moves to automation.

briefs.headline: OpenAI says its first chip beats Nvidia's best per watt
briefs.summary: The Jalapeno inference chip ran 1.5 to 1.9 times more work per watt than Blackwell on three open models in SemiAnalysis benchmarks — though its newer memory flatters the comparison.

art.caption: Buildings stand alone in the mud-choked Trishuli valley after the flood swept the ground from around them.

weather_ear: The Weatherman has the forecast at 7:15.
kicker: The away desk and Vacation Hotspots carry their first lines this morning; the Mid-Ohio Valley, Nicholas and Summers were quiet.
